Symptoms:

Signup's Availability SLO monitor (154229727) is still in Alert state (7-day error-budget burn metric, doesn't self-clear on the same timescale as the rest).

Trace IDs: none captured (metric-only re-investigation this cycle, no fresh APM trace pull)

Suggested next action: ops to confirm SQL/network root cause on clusters c2/c3/c4; once confirmed, finalize kb candidate ki-2026-07-06-sql-cluster-c2c3c4-error40-cascade (proposed, not yet written) — recommend folding signup into that same entry rather than a separate one

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (SQL cluster c2/c3/c4 connectivity cascade)
Source: #team-incident-response SWAT runbook · critical-path impact · 8+ services
Owning teams (would tag — not tagged): `@admin` (auth/identity/gateway/search), `CRM` (scheduler/rt-core-subscriber), `@no code next gen` (runtime-designer); SQL clusters c2/c3/c4 → infra/DBA

Symptoms:
  • TCP error-40 "Could not open a connection to SQL Server" on sql.connection_c2/c3/c4 from ~01:26–02:18 UTC, cascading 5xx across all SQL-dependent services
  • ms-authentication-api + ms-identity-api (critical path) still elevated at 02:22 UTC — new sessions failing
  • runtime-designer restart (02:17Z) hung on startup, then self-recovered; the SWAT alert scoped it to one host but the root cause is cluster-wide SQL

Likely cause: SQL-tier / network-path reachability loss to clusters c2/c3/c4 (error 40 = TCP-level unreachable, not a deploy). Do NOT keep restarting designercoreapi — it blocks on SQL at startup.
Suggested next action: check SQL hosts backing c2/c3/c4 (up? accepting remote TCP?) + app-tier→SQL-tier network path (SG/firewall/route/DNS ~01:20–01:40Z); prioritize auth/identity over the runtime-designer host.

  - ES confirms mechanism: Redis Cache Circuit Breaker OPENED 13:23:28Z (StackExchange.Redis.RedisConnectionException), plus 87 cache-operation-failure log lines (REMOVE/GET/SET/key-fetch) in the same window
  - Cross-service: runtime-core-api independently logged 9 Redis errors ("Redis operation cancelled" x7, "timed out after 5s" x2) in the same window, and its own RTC p95 monitor fired 13:49:21Z (peak 9.62s) — first confirmed cross-service Redis correlation between this new finding and known-issue ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring (posted separately this cycle)

Trace IDs: dd_trace_id 6a4bae4300000000f629ba016a5d255e (RequestPath /v1/field/SaveViewBundleInternal, coincidental null-ref trace, not the latency driver)
Likely cause: Transient Redis connectivity blip caused a client-side circuit-breaker open on ms-tables-fields-api; cache-fallback to uncached reads drove p95 latency up for ~5 minutes, self-recovered
Suggested next action: monitor — no Method code fix identified; if recurs, escalate to infra/DBA-adjacent on-call to check Redis/ElastiCache health during 13:20-13:26Z. New KB entry written: `ki-2026-07-06-tables-fields-redis-circuitbreaker-p95-latency`
